Let $n = 2016$. Call a valid integer $k$ *balanced* if every $k\times k$ contiguous sub-block contains exactly $k$ Active panels. Let $S$ be the set of balanced protocols.

**Construction (lower bound: 1008).**

Make column $c = 1008$ entirely Active, and every other panel Inactive. For any $k$ with $1009 \le k \le 2016$, consider an arbitrary $k\times k$ block occupying rows $[i,i+k-1]$ and columns $[j,j+k-1]$. The set of column-ranges over all valid $j\in\{1,\dots,n-k+1\}$ is $\{[j,j+k-1]\}$; their intersection is
$$\bigcap_{j=1}^{n-k+1}[j,j+k-1]=[n-k+1,\,k].$$
For $k\ge 1009$ we have $n-k+1 = 2017-k \le 1008 \le k$, so $c=1008$ lies in every column-range. Hence every $k\times k$ block contains the single active column $c$, contributing exactly $k$ active panels (one per row of the block), and no other active panels. So every such block sums to $k$.

For $k\le 1008$, the block with columns $[1009, 1008+k]\subseteq[1009,2016]$ (valid since $1008+k\le 2016$) avoids column $1008$ entirely, so its sum is $0\neq k$. Thus exactly the values $k\in\{1009,1010,\dots,2016\}$ are balanced — a total of $2016-1009+1=1008$ protocols.

**Upper bound (at most 1008).**

We first establish a key constraint between any two balanced values. Suppose $k_1 < k_2$ are both balanced. Take any $k_2\times k_2$ block; it contains exactly $k_2$ Active panels. Inside it, place as many **disjoint** $k_1\times k_1$ sub-blocks as possible, aligned on a $k_1$-grid: this yields $\lfloor k_2/k_1\rfloor^2$ disjoint $k_1\times k_1$ blocks (positions $(a+pk_1,\,b+qk_1)$ for $0\le p,q < \lfloor k_2/k_1\rfloor$), each fully contained since $\lfloor k_2/k_1\rfloor\cdot k_1\le k_2$. Each such sub-block sums to $k_1$ (because $k_1$ is balanced). Being disjoint subsets of a block with only $k_2$ Active panels,
$$\left\lfloor\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right\rfloor^{\!2}\!k_1 \;\le\; k_2. \tag{$\star$}$$

Let $q=\lfloor k_2/k_1\rfloor$. If $q\ge 2$, then $q^2\ge q+1$ (since $q^2-q-1\ge 1$ for $q\ge 2$), so $q^2 k_1 \ge (q+1)k_1 > k_2$ (because $k_2 < (q+1)k_1$ by definition of floor), contradicting $(\star)$. Therefore $q=1$, i.e.
$$k_2 < 2k_1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k_1 > \tfrac{k_2}{2}.$$

Let $m = \max S$ (so $m\le n = 2016$). Applying the constraint with $k_2=m$: every balanced $k_1$ satisfies $k_1 > m/2$. Hence
$$S \subseteq \bigl(\tfrac{m}{2},\, m\bigr]\cap\mathbb{Z},$$
which contains at most $m - \lfloor m/2\rfloor = \lceil m/2\rceil$ integers. Therefore
$$|S|\le \left\lceil\frac{m}{2}\right\rceil \le \left\lceil\frac{2016}{2}\right\rceil = 1008.$$

**Conclusion.** The construction achieves 1008 balanced protocols, and no configuration can exceed 1008. The maximum possible number of Balanced protocols is

$$\boxed{1008}.$$
